RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation for Account Executives
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session huddle motion, where AI reduces AE preparation and reporting work, which tools may appear, and what to review before next week's topic.
TodayObjective: Understand how the AE huddle path runs and where the human checkpoints protect account, deal, and forecast judgment.
Wiifm: You are not being asked to learn another tool for its own sake. You are being asked to reclaim time from prep, reporting, and chasing context so more of your week goes to customers and decisions.
DesiredOutcome: AEs know how the huddle motion works, which tools may show up, what to review, and what AI experiences to bring back before next week.

RoleTopicName: Prioritize Accounts and Build an Actionable Account Plan
RoleTopicDescription: Turn customer priorities, pipeline, renewals, whitespace, partner coverage, and investment signals into a short account plan built on decisions rather than an inventory.
TodayObjective: Turn scattered account context into a short, evidence-backed action plan for the accounts that most deserve attention now.
Wiifm: Account plans often become static documents. This turns yours into a weekly operating list tied to customer outcomes, pipeline movement, and renewal risk.
DesiredOutcome: A prioritized account list with the reason for priority, source signals, role gaps, and one named next action for each top account.

RoleTopicName: Inspect Pipeline Signal Quality and Restore Trust
RoleTopicDescription: Use certified business data and MSX context to find where pipeline quality, stage evidence, dates, or next steps misrepresent reality.
TodayObjective: Find where the pipeline signal is wrong, incomplete, or misleading before it becomes a forecast problem.
Wiifm: The easiest forecast conversation is the one where the data is already clean enough to discuss decisions instead of defending the spreadsheet.
DesiredOutcome: A short list of pipeline hygiene fixes, stale or at-risk opportunities, source signals, and seller-owned corrections or follow-ups.

RoleTopicName: Build a Decision-Ready Forecast Narrative
RoleTopicDescription: Turn pipeline movement, risks, committed deals, and forecast changes into a narrative that holds up to manager and Area inspection.
TodayObjective: Convert pipeline movement and risk into a forecast narrative that explains the position, not just the number.
Wiifm: A forecast is an argument about what will happen and why. AI can assemble the evidence, but you own the judgment and the commitment.
DesiredOutcome: A forecast narrative with sourced movement, at-risk commits, gap drivers, open inspection questions, and follow-up actions.

RoleTopicName: Create and Qualify New Opportunities from Buying Signals
RoleTopicDescription: Convert customer signals, whitespace, meetings, engagement, and account context into qualified opportunities while separating evidence from optimism.
TodayObjective: Find one real opportunity signal, test whether it is qualified, and define the next customer action.
Wiifm: Pipeline gaps are usually discovery gaps. This finds opportunities already hiding in accounts you own, without creating noise in MSX.
DesiredOutcome: At least one qualified opportunity hypothesis with the trigger, evidence, stakeholder, next action, and unresolved assumptions named.

RoleTopicName: Prepare an Executive Customer Conversation and Value Narrative
RoleTopicDescription: Synthesize account context, open commitments, stakeholder dynamics, value evidence, and likely objections into a decision-moving customer conversation.
TodayObjective: Prepare for a live customer conversation with the outcome, evidence, talking points, objections, and ask made explicit.
Wiifm: Calendar pressure makes preparation the first thing to shrink. This makes preparation fast enough to happen without falling back on generic talking points.
DesiredOutcome: A conversation brief with source signals, relationship nuance, likely objections, CXO-ready talking points, a primary ask, and a fallback ask.

RoleTopicName: Inspect Deal Health and Accelerate the Next Decision
RoleTopicDescription: Work stage evidence, exit criteria, approvals, commercial dependencies, and account-team ownership into the next real customer decision.
TodayObjective: Move a live deal from general urgency to the next governed decision, with blockers, roles, and evidence visible.
Wiifm: Deals rarely stall because nobody cares. They stall because the next decision, blocker, or owner is fuzzy. This makes the fuzzy part inspectable.
DesiredOutcome: A deal inspection brief with the next decision, risks, approval or role gaps, customer follow-up, and owners for the next actions.

RoleTopicName: Manage Renewal Risk and Expansion Readiness
RoleTopicDescription: Read renewal timing, consumption and usage gaps, value evidence, recent engagement, and commercial review needs early enough to change the outcome.
TodayObjective: Identify the largest renewal risk early enough to act, and connect expansion to evidenced customer value.
Wiifm: A renewal is decided long before the renewal date. Seeing risk and value evidence early gives you time to change the result.
DesiredOutcome: A renewal view with risk evidence, value proof gaps, expansion hypothesis, account-team owners, and a customer-ready next action.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session huddle motion, where AI reduces ATS research and planning work, which tools may appear, and what to review before next week's topic.
TodayObjective: Understand how the ATS huddle path runs and where AI fits technical strategy and account planning.
Wiifm: Technical strategy work is where AI either saves real time or wastes it. This is where you find out which.
DesiredOutcome: ATSs know how the huddle motion works, which tools may show up, what to review, and what AI experiences to bring back before next week.

RoleTopicName: Build an Account Intelligence and Meeting Prep Brief
RoleTopicDescription: Build the current account, stakeholder, KPI, workload, and risk context needed before committing to a technical direction.
TodayObjective: Create the evidence base behind your account technology decisions.
Wiifm: You are asked to justify technical priorities to people who did not see the evidence. This carries the evidence with you.
DesiredOutcome: An account intelligence brief with technical risks, workload signals, stakeholder context, and next actions.

RoleTopicName: Assemble an Executive Technical Customer Narrative
RoleTopicDescription: Translate architecture, risk, roadmap, proof, and business value into an executive-ready technical story with a clear ask.
TodayObjective: Turn account intelligence into a technical story an executive can act on.
Wiifm: Executives do not buy architecture. They buy a consequence. This connects the technical path to that consequence.
DesiredOutcome: An executive-ready technical narrative with sourced claims, proof points, decision questions, and a technical ask.

RoleTopicName: Prioritize AI and Azure Workloads by Readiness and Impact
RoleTopicDescription: Rank the AI and Azure workloads that deserve technical focus using readiness, impact, upside, dependencies, and ownership.
TodayObjective: Cut the workload list down to the few that are genuinely ready, genuinely owned, and worth your technical time this quarter.
Wiifm: Not every promising workload is ready, valuable, or owned. Prioritization keeps technical strategy from becoming a wish list.
DesiredOutcome: A ranked workload view with readiness, impact, evidence, owner, and validation gaps.

RoleTopicName: Develop a Technical Strategy and Decision Trajectory
RoleTopicDescription: Connect customer objectives, estate, architecture direction, risks, bets, proof needs, and roadmap into a sequenced technical decision path.
TodayObjective: Set the technical direction and the sequence of decisions that gets the customer there.
Wiifm: Technical strategy without a decision sequence is a diagram. The sequence is what makes it actionable.
DesiredOutcome: A technical trajectory with priority bets, proof needs, owners, risks, milestones, and open decisions.

RoleTopicName: Design an Executive Briefing Experience
RoleTopicDescription: Design an executive briefing that advances specific customer decisions and prepares the right participants, evidence, roles, timeline, and follow-through.
TodayObjective: Turn technical strategy into a purposeful executive experience.
Wiifm: A briefing is not a deck. It is a designed decision moment with the right people, evidence, and follow-through.
DesiredOutcome: An EBC plan with desired decisions, participants, evidence, preparation milestones, and follow-through ownership.

RoleTopicName: Adjust the Technical Talk Track from Customer Signals
RoleTopicDescription: Adapt the technical conversation to current customer signals, likely questions, objections, and the decision in front of the customer.
TodayObjective: Update the technical talk track before the customer hears it.
Wiifm: The best technical story still fails when it ignores the latest customer signal.
DesiredOutcome: A signal-adjusted talk track with opening language, questions, objections, responses, and human review flags.

RoleTopicName: Mobilize the Technical V-Team Around Priorities and Risks
RoleTopicDescription: Align technical roles, owners, dependencies, investment signals, risks, and follow-through around the customer decision.
TodayObjective: Get the technical v-team and partners moving on the same priority, with clear handoffs.
Wiifm: You have responsibility without authority. Explicit handoffs are the substitute for authority.
DesiredOutcome: A technical v-team alignment brief with owners, dependencies, investment signals, checkpoints, and next actions.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session huddle motion, where AI reduces specialist assembly work, which tools may appear, and what to review before next week's topic.
TodayObjective: Understand how the SSP huddle path runs and where AI fits solution pursuit, with human judgment explicit.
Wiifm: Specialist time is scarce. This motion is designed to cut assembly work so more of it goes to customer decisions and solution-area growth.
DesiredOutcome: SSPs know how the huddle motion works, which tools may show up, what to review, and what AI experiences to bring back before next week.

RoleTopicName: Prioritize Prospects and Follow Up on Leads
RoleTopicDescription: Turn event, lead, account, and buying signals into a ranked solution-area follow-up plan with a named owner for each top prospect.
TodayObjective: Turn noisy lead and account signals into a ranked follow-up plan you can work today.
Wiifm: You stop guessing which prospects deserve the next hour, and you stop losing warm leads to inbox decay.
DesiredOutcome: A ranked prospect list with a specific next action and owner for the top five.

RoleTopicName: Build a Solution-Selling Plan
RoleTopicDescription: Shape a solution play into a repeatable pursuit plan covering target accounts, stakeholder coverage, proof needs, and the demo or workshop sequence.
TodayObjective: Shape the solution play into a plan with customer outcomes, proof, owners, and the next decision.
Wiifm: Specialists are pulled in every direction. A written plan lets you focus the right pursuits and say no to the wrong ones.
DesiredOutcome: A solution-selling plan with customer outcomes, stakeholder coverage, proof needs, and a 30-day progression plan.

RoleTopicName: Develop a Customer-Specific Value Narrative
RoleTopicDescription: Translate the solution into the customer's own priorities, evidence, caveats, and next ask.
TodayObjective: Build the value logic before customer-facing execution, using evidence the customer will recognize.
Wiifm: Generic value decks lose to specific ones. This is how you build the specific story quickly and responsibly.
DesiredOutcome: A review-ready value narrative tied to customer priorities, proof, assumptions, and next ask.

RoleTopicName: Prepare a Solution-Specific Customer Conversation
RoleTopicDescription: Prepare the discovery questions, proof, objections, role contributions, and ask that move a solution conversation to a decision.
TodayObjective: Prepare and rehearse the solution conversation so it advances a decision rather than explaining a product.
Wiifm: Specialists get pulled into meetings with no defined outcome. Preparing the decision you are driving changes that.
DesiredOutcome: A solution conversation plan with discovery questions, proof, objections, role contributions, and next ask.

RoleTopicName: Orchestrate the Specialist, Technical Team, Partners, and Funding
RoleTopicDescription: Coordinate specialists, technical contributors, partner inputs, and funding dependencies into a resourced pursuit plan with confirmed timing.
TodayObjective: Mobilize the right people, partners, and funding path around the customer objective and next decision.
Wiifm: Pursuits stall waiting for a resource, partner input, or funding step nobody formally owned. This makes the ask explicit.
DesiredOutcome: A coordinated pursuit plan with roles, dependencies, partner and funding needs, owners, and decision checkpoints.

RoleTopicName: Develop a Competitive Position and Response Plan
RoleTopicDescription: Build proof-backed differentiation, objection handling, and risk response for the competitive position in front of you.
TodayObjective: Build the competitive position once customer context, value logic, and solution intent are clear.
Wiifm: Competitive conversations are lost by improvisation. A prepared, evidenced position is the difference.
DesiredOutcome: A competitive position with differentiators, proof, objections, risks, and response plan.

RoleTopicName: Advance the Solution Opportunity and Clear the Next Decision
RoleTopicDescription: Work milestone readiness, stakeholder gaps, proof, blockers, dependencies, and commitments into the next customer decision.
TodayObjective: Translate the solution strategy into deal progression and a measurable next customer decision.
Wiifm: A pursuit is not advanced until the next decision, owner, and evidence are named.
DesiredOutcome: A readiness view with blockers, next decision, owners, and a 14- to 30-day action plan.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session huddle motion, where AI reduces SE rework on proof and response work, which tools may appear, and what to review before next week's topic.
TodayObjective: Understand how the SE huddle path runs and which human checkpoints protect technical accuracy.
Wiifm: You are not being asked to outsource judgment. You are being asked to use AI to assemble evidence, pressure-test assumptions, and make technical decisions easier to review.
DesiredOutcome: SEs know how the huddle motion works, which tools may show up, what to review, and what AI experiences to bring back before next week.

RoleTopicName: Produce a Grounded Technical Response
RoleTopicDescription: Respond to RFPs, questionnaires, and technical asks with sourced answers, confidence levels, assumptions, exceptions, and SME-needed flags.
TodayObjective: Create a governed technical response that separates supported answers from assumptions and routes open items to the right reviewer.
Wiifm: The risky part of technical response work is not writing. It is knowing which claims are supported, which are uncertain, and who must review them.
DesiredOutcome: A grounded technical answer matrix and response package with unresolved items, confidence flags, and reviewer assignments.

RoleTopicName: Design and Validate the Customer Architecture
RoleTopicDescription: Translate discovery criteria into architecture options, assumptions, risks, validation steps, and an architecture decision record.
TodayObjective: Compare architecture options against the customer decision criteria and document the recommended direction with risks and validation needs.
Wiifm: Architecture debates get faster when the options, criteria, assumptions, and proof needs are visible before the meeting.
DesiredOutcome: A reviewed architecture decision record with options, criteria, risks, dependencies, and validation steps.

RoleTopicName: Design a Demo or Workshop That Advances the Decision
RoleTopicDescription: Create a focused demo or workshop experience that proves the most important customer scenario and produces a next decision.
TodayObjective: Build a demo or workshop plan around the customer decision, not around the full feature set.
Wiifm: A demo that tries to show everything often proves nothing. This narrows the experience to the evidence the customer needs to decide.
DesiredOutcome: A demo or workshop plan with scenario, audience, decision criteria, evidence, objections, roles, and fallback path.

RoleTopicName: Scope a PoC with Success and Exit Criteria
RoleTopicDescription: Define the smallest useful proof, success measures, milestones, owners, dependencies, review gates, and exit decision.
TodayObjective: Turn a proposed PoC into a bounded proof with explicit success criteria and a clear exit decision.
Wiifm: A PoC without exit criteria becomes a project. The value is knowing what proof is enough before work starts.
DesiredOutcome: A PoC plan with in-scope scenario, success and exit criteria, milestones, dependencies, owners, and handoff path.

RoleTopicName: Lead Technical Discovery and Define Decision Criteria
RoleTopicDescription: Use approved customer and technical context to turn discovery into agreed decision criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision.
TodayObjective: Convert an upcoming discovery conversation into a decision-ready brief with bounded problem, constraints, evidence gaps, and customer decision criteria.
Wiifm: Better discovery prevents second discovery meetings. The payoff is a clearer customer decision and fewer surprises during architecture, demo, or PoC work.
DesiredOutcome: A discovery brief with agreed decision criteria, open evidence gaps, and the next technical action.

RoleTopicName: Manage Technical Risk and Advance the Deal
RoleTopicDescription: Inspect exit criteria, proof gaps, blockers, objections, dependencies, and the next technical decision needed to progress the opportunity.
TodayObjective: Name the technical risk holding the deal, identify the evidence needed to clear it, and assign the next technical action.
Wiifm: Deals often wait on a technical answer nobody has explicitly owned. This makes the blocker, owner, and evidence need visible.
DesiredOutcome: A technical risk and handoff plan with blocker, impact, owner, mitigation, checkpoint, and next decision.

RoleTopicName: Capture and Reuse Technical Assets and Learning
RoleTopicDescription: Convert proven patterns, demos, scripts, architectures, responses, and lessons into reusable assets or Skill Blueprints with context and safeguards.
TodayObjective: Package one piece of technical work so another SE can find, trust, adapt, and reuse it.
Wiifm: SEs rebuild useful work because the original lacks context, ownership, or searchability. Capture saves future technical time.
DesiredOutcome: One reusable technical asset or Skill Blueprint with purpose, prerequisites, parameters, limitations, owner, and validation checks.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session huddle motion, where AI supports commercial work, where its boundaries sit, which tools may appear, and what to review before next week's topic.
TodayObjective: Understand how the CE huddle path runs and where the boundaries sit for AI in commercial work.
Wiifm: Commercial work has the least tolerance for AI error. This session sets out where the boundaries are before you rely on anything.
DesiredOutcome: CEs know how the huddle motion works, which tools may show up, what to review, and what AI experiences to bring back before next week.

RoleTopicName: Prioritize Commercial Risk and Intervention
RoleTopicDescription: Surface the commercial risk, structural exposure, and authoritative-source questions that would otherwise appear at approval.
TodayObjective: Find the commercial risk that will surface at approval, and decide the intervention while it is still cheap.
Wiifm: Commercial risk found at approval is a delay. Found earlier, it becomes a structuring decision you can still influence.
DesiredOutcome: A prioritized commercial risk view with intervention, owner, and authoritative source for each item.

RoleTopicName: Develop Commercial Options and Approval Path (1 of 3)
RoleTopicDescription: Compare viable commercial structures and map the approval requirements each one triggers, before the negotiation starts.
TodayObjective: Find the structure that is both commercially right and actually approvable, before you are committed to defending one.
Wiifm: Structure decides whether a deal is approvable. Seeing the trade-offs and approval route early prevents rework later.
DesiredOutcome: A commercial options matrix with trade-offs, risks, approval requirements, and open decisions.

RoleTopicName: Build the Commercial Decision Narrative (2 of 3)
RoleTopicDescription: Turn approved commercial context into an internal recommendation and a customer-specific transition brief.
TodayObjective: Make the recommendation reviewable, so the reviewer spends their time deciding rather than reconstructing your reasoning.
Wiifm: A clear recommendation makes review faster, because the options, assumptions, and risks are visible instead of rediscovered.
DesiredOutcome: A recommended commercial path with assumptions, reviewers, transition impacts, and next decision named.

RoleTopicName: Prepare and Lead the Commercial Negotiation (3 of 3)
RoleTopicDescription: Build the negotiation position, concession logic, authority boundaries, and validated deal path for customer-facing use.
TodayObjective: Prepare the negotiation so give-and-get logic and authority limits are settled before customer pressure arrives.
Wiifm: Negotiations are where vague structure becomes expensive. Preparing give-and-get logic and authority boundaries keeps judgment human-led.
DesiredOutcome: A negotiation plan and validated deal path with authority, concessions, escalation triggers, and review flags.

RoleTopicName: Orchestrate Commercial Approvals and Execution
RoleTopicDescription: Route approval handoffs, exception cases, investment dependencies, and commercial execution to named owners.
TodayObjective: Replace every implied approval owner on this deal with a named one.
Wiifm: Commercial execution stalls when approval ownership is implied. Naming the route, owner, evidence, and blocker keeps the deal moving without overstating authority.
DesiredOutcome: A governed commercial execution plan with approval owners, handoffs, blockers, and the next decision clear.

RoleTopicName: Build and Execute the Commercial Renewal Strategy
RoleTopicDescription: Work renewal economics, commercial structure, risk, expansion potential, and approval path into a renewal strategy.
TodayObjective: Decide what you are actually trying to achieve at this renewal, before the customer sets the agenda for you.
Wiifm: Renewals are commercial events, not administrative ones. Treating them as strategy is where risk, margin, and expansion become visible.
DesiredOutcome: A renewal strategy with commercial risk, structure, expansion potential, approval path, and next decision named.

RoleTopicName: Validate Policy, Licensing, and Approval Boundaries
RoleTopicDescription: Check eligibility questions, licensing risk, and approval routing against authoritative guidance before deal structure hardens.
TodayObjective: Check policy, licensing, and approval boundaries before structuring decisions harden.
Wiifm: Policy questions found at approval cost weeks. Found before structure and negotiation, they cost a conversation.
DesiredOutcome: A policy and licensing check with every open question routed to its authoritative owner before the deal path is locked.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session huddle motion, where AI reduces CSA delivery and architecture assembly work, which tools may appear, and what to review before next week's topic.
TodayObjective: Understand how the CSA huddle path runs and where AI fits customer architecture and delivery.
Wiifm: You inherit whatever is designed and delivered upstream. This explains where you get a say earlier.
DesiredOutcome: CSAs know how the huddle motion works, which tools may show up, what to review, and what AI experiences to bring back before next week.

RoleTopicName: Forecast Consumption and Intervene on Technical Risk
RoleTopicDescription: Compare consumption against plan, trace each gap to its technical cause, and select the intervention that changes the trajectory.
TodayObjective: Find where the consumption gap is technically caused, and start one intervention while it still matters.
Wiifm: Consumption shortfalls get raised to you after they show up in a report. This is how you see them while there is still time.
DesiredOutcome: A consumption position with the technical causes named and one intervention owned.

RoleTopicName: Prepare a Technical Advisory Conversation
RoleTopicDescription: Prepare the recommendation, supporting evidence, and decision request that turn an advisory conversation into a customer decision.
TodayObjective: Prepare the advisory conversation so the customer leaves with a decision, not a list of options.
Wiifm: Advisory conversations drift into education when they are not prepared. Preparation is what keeps them advisory.
DesiredOutcome: An advisory plan with the recommendation, the evidence, and the decision you are asking for.

RoleTopicName: Design a Production-Ready Architecture and Validation Path (1 of 2)
RoleTopicDescription: Compare production architecture options against customer constraints, then turn the chosen direction into a documented design with a validation and proof plan.
TodayObjective: Commit to one architecture direction, and say plainly what evidence would prove it wrong.
Wiifm: You inherit what was designed pre-sale. Designing for production now is how you avoid absorbing it later.
DesiredOutcome: A production-ready architecture package with the decision path, validation plan, and dependencies named.

RoleTopicName: Validate the Architecture Evidence and Confirm Delivery Readiness (2 of 2)
RoleTopicDescription: Pressure-test the architecture evidence, confirm delivery readiness for investment-funded scope, and plan the interventions the design still needs.
TodayObjective: Find the part of this design that has not actually been proven, while it is still cheap to fix.
Wiifm: A design that has not been evidence-checked becomes someone else's escalation. Validating now is cheaper than defending it later.
DesiredOutcome: A validated architecture evidence base with delivery-readiness findings and an owned intervention plan.

RoleTopicName: Assess Technical Health and Prioritize Risk
RoleTopicDescription: Rank technical risk by how likely it is to become customer-visible, with evidence and owners attached to each item.
TodayObjective: Pick the one technical risk you would least like the customer to find first, and start on it today.
Wiifm: Technical risk you catch this week is a conversation. The same risk found by the customer is an escalation.
DesiredOutcome: A ranked technical risk list with evidence, owners, and one intervention started.

RoleTopicName: Optimize Cost and Build the FinOps Recommendation (1 of 2)
RoleTopicDescription: Build the cost and consumption evidence base, then turn it into a costed optimization recommendation the customer can act on.
TodayObjective: Find the cost the customer is not seeing, and turn it into a defensible optimization recommendation.
Wiifm: FinOps findings buy credibility. A concrete saving is the fastest way to be trusted on the larger technical argument.
DesiredOutcome: A validated optimization evidence base with one costed FinOps recommendation and an owned intervention plan.

RoleTopicName: Translate Technical Progress into a Customer Value Narrative (2 of 2)
RoleTopicDescription: Turn technical progress into a value story the customer recognizes, with the evidence behind every claim checked before it is shown.
TodayObjective: Connect technical progress to the outcome the customer asked for, using evidence that survives scrutiny.
Wiifm: Technical work is only credited when someone connects it to what the customer wanted. Unverified claims lose that credit instantly.
DesiredOutcome: A customer-ready technical value narrative and review package with each claim evidence-checked.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session huddle motion, where AI reduces CSAM status-assembly work, which tools may appear, and what to review before next week's topic.
TodayObjective: Understand how the CSAM huddle path runs and where AI fits the customer-success work you already do.
Wiifm: You are not being asked to become a tool demo person. You are being given a way to spend less time assembling status and more time driving customer outcomes.
DesiredOutcome: CSAMs know how the huddle motion works, which tools may show up, what to review, and what AI experiences to bring back before next week.

RoleTopicName: Build Outcome-Anchored Success Plans
RoleTopicDescription: Turn customer priorities into an executable success plan with outcomes, milestones, owners, risks, and review points.
TodayObjective: Start with the customer outcome and build the plan that makes progress observable.
Wiifm: Success plans decay when they become inventories. This turns the plan into a living operating system for customer value.
DesiredOutcome: A refreshed success-plan view with outcomes, milestones, owners, risks, and the next review point named.

RoleTopicName: Assess Customer Health and Predict Risks
RoleTopicDescription: Combine health, usage, support, sentiment, delivery, and stakeholder signals into a ranked risk view with a chosen intervention.
TodayObjective: Move from health scores to the next intervention that changes customer trajectory.
Wiifm: Risk found early is a customer conversation. Risk found late is an escalation with an audience.
DesiredOutcome: A ranked health and risk view with one active intervention, owner, due date, and escalation threshold.

RoleTopicName: Map Stakeholders and Drive Executive Alignment
RoleTopicDescription: Map sponsors, decision makers, workload owners, and relationship risks, then prepare the executive alignment narrative.
TodayObjective: Prepare the stakeholder conversation that aligns priorities, decisions, and sponsorship.
Wiifm: A strong CSAM does not only track activity. They keep the right people aligned before value or risk becomes invisible.
DesiredOutcome: A stakeholder map and executive alignment brief with relationship risks, message, evidence, and next ask.

RoleTopicName: Orchestrate Microsoft, Partners and Customer Teams
RoleTopicDescription: Turn scattered workstreams into a clear operating rhythm across customer stakeholders, Microsoft roles, partners, support, and delivery.
TodayObjective: Make the customer-success system easier to run by making handoffs and decisions explicit.
Wiifm: Most work stalls in the handoff, not the task. Orchestration is how CSAMs create speed without owning every action.
DesiredOutcome: A v-team orchestration brief with workstreams, owners, inputs, decisions, dates, and escalations.

RoleTopicName: Accelerate Adoption and Prove Value Realization
RoleTopicDescription: Identify adoption friction, connect usage to customer outcomes, and prepare a value story the customer recognizes.
TodayObjective: Turn adoption signals into value proof and the next behavior-change intervention.
Wiifm: Adoption without value evidence is fragile. Value that is not communicated is invisible at renewal.
DesiredOutcome: A four-week adoption and value plan with gaps, actions, owners, milestones, and customer-ready value evidence.

RoleTopicName: Forecast Consumption, Renewal and Growth Opportunities
RoleTopicDescription: Connect consumption trajectory, usage commitments, adoption gaps, value evidence, and stakeholder health to renewal and expansion readiness.
TodayObjective: See renewal and growth conditions early enough to improve them.
Wiifm: Renewal readiness is built by value evidence over time, not assembled at the deadline.
DesiredOutcome: A renewal and growth readiness view with top risk, value proof, consumption gap, expansion hypothesis, and v-team next action.

RoleTopicName: Lead Delivery Risks, Escalations and Recovery Plans
RoleTopicDescription: Build a grounded brief for incidents, delivery risks, overdue milestones, and the recovery actions that answer them.
TodayObjective: Turn escalation noise into a recovery plan with accountability and customer-safe communication.
Wiifm: Escalations test trust. A grounded brief reduces chasing, avoids surprises, and keeps the customer conversation focused on recovery.
DesiredOutcome: A recovery plan with impact, owners, decisions, next actions, communication cadence, and follow-through mechanism.

RoleTopicName: Action the Signals That Are About to Expire
RoleTopicDescription: Work the Contact Me signals and preloaded Plan Priorities you own against their windows, and decide deliberately which ones you are not going to work.
TodayObjective: Triage your current signal queue, action the one closest to expiry, and record a decision on the ones you are letting go.
Wiifm: Signals expire quietly and the ones you never looked at count against you the same as the ones you declined. This is how you stop losing them by accident.
DesiredOutcome: A triaged queue with expiring signals identified, one signal actioned, and an explicit decision on everything you are not pursuing.

RoleTopicName: Hand Over Well and Stay on the Clock
RoleTopicDescription: Choose what genuinely goes to a partner, package it inside the data-sharing rules, and track it through acceptance and conversion instead of assuming it is handled.
TodayObjective: Send one referral with what the partner actually needs, and get a clear read on where your existing referrals sit against their windows.
Wiifm: A referral nobody accepted expires on its own and takes the coverage with it. This is how you find that out while you can still do something.
DesiredOutcome: One well-packaged referral sent, a read on your open referrals against the acceptance and conversion windows, and one stalled referral chased or closed.

RoleTopicName: Decide Who Is Actually Covering Each Account
RoleTopicDescription: Segment a territory you cannot work account by account into what you cover, what a partner covers and what nobody covers, then take the uncovered part into the joint plan instead of leaving it to chance.
TodayObjective: Produce an honest coverage read on your territory and name the accounts currently covered by nobody.
Wiifm: The accounts that lapse are almost never the ones you decided to drop. They are the ones that were never on anybody's list, and you find out at renewal.
DesiredOutcome: A territory segmented by actual coverage, the uncovered accounts named, and one of them either taken on or deliberately routed to a partner.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation for Digital Account Executives
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session huddle motion, where AI reduces the preparation and triage load across a territory of roughly fifty accounts, which tools may appear, and what to bring back each week.
TodayObjective: Understand how the DAE huddle path runs and where the human checkpoints protect territory, partner and deal judgment.
Wiifm: You are not being asked to learn another tool. You are being asked to get time back from triage and preparation across a territory nobody could work account by account.
DesiredOutcome: DAEs know how the motion works, which tools may show up, and what to try before the next session.

RoleTopicName: Prepare a Frontier Conversation Without a Week of Research
RoleTopicDescription: Prepare a customer conversation that moves a decision when the account is one of roughly fifty and the preparation time available is measured in minutes rather than days.
TodayObjective: Prepare one customer conversation to a standard you could not reach manually in the time you actually have.
Wiifm: At this account load the honest choice is usually between a generic conversation and no conversation. This is how preparation becomes fast enough to happen.
DesiredOutcome: A prepared conversation with a stated outcome, the likely objection anticipated, and the evidence ready.

RoleTopicName: Advance a Deal Somebody Else May Close
RoleTopicDescription: Move a deal to its next decision when a partner is frequently the one transacting it, which changes what you can see, what you control and what you have to ask for.
TodayObjective: Establish where one deal actually sits when part of the motion is happening outside your systems.
Wiifm: A deal a partner is closing looks stalled in MSX right up until it closes. Knowing the difference between quiet and stuck is the skill.
DesiredOutcome: The next decision named, what you can see separated from what you are assuming, and one specific ask made of the partner or the customer.

RoleTopicName: Work the Renewal Book Before It Reaches You
RoleTopicDescription: Run the renewal workback across a book of agreements rather than a single account, and find the mid-term expansion that is easier to land than a new logo.
TodayObjective: Find the renewal in your book that needs work now rather than the one with the nearest date.
Wiifm: Renewals arrive in a queue and get worked in date order, which is almost never risk order. The one that surprises you was always visible earlier.
DesiredOutcome: A renewal book sorted by risk rather than by date, with one at-risk renewal actioned and one expansion hypothesis tested.

RoleTopicName: Read Portfolio Health Without Inspecting Every Account
RoleTopicDescription: Find the accounts moving in the wrong direction across a portfolio too large to inspect individually, and decide which movement is worth your own time.
TodayObjective: Identify the accounts whose direction of travel changed, and act on one.
Wiifm: At this coverage ratio you will not notice an account going wrong by looking at it. You notice by watching what moved.
DesiredOutcome: The accounts that changed direction identified, the movement explained rather than assumed, and one intervention started.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation for Commercial Executives in SME&C
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session motion, where AI reduces the commercial research and preparation load across a book of agreements rather than a handful, and what to bring back each week.
TodayObjective: Understand how the CE path runs in this segment and where the human checkpoints protect commercial and policy judgment.
Wiifm: Commercial work here is spread across far more agreements than anyone can inspect individually, and much of it transacts through a partner. This is about getting the research time back.
DesiredOutcome: CEs know how the motion works, which tools may show up, and what to try before the next session.

RoleTopicName: Run the Renewal Workback Across a Book, Not an Account
RoleTopicDescription: Work an always-on renewal workback across many agreements at once, decide which ones need a commercial intervention, and start early enough that the structure is still open.
TodayObjective: Find the renewals in your book where a commercial decision is still available, rather than the ones that are nearly due.
Wiifm: By the time a renewal is in its final quarter, most of the commercial options have closed. The value you add is almost entirely a function of when you arrive.
DesiredOutcome: A renewal book sorted by where commercial intervention is still possible, with one workback started.

RoleTopicName: Shape a Deal the Partner Will Transact
RoleTopicDescription: Get the commercial structure right on a deal a partner will actually sell and invoice, where your influence runs through advice and enablement rather than through execution.
TodayObjective: Establish what you can actually influence on a partner-transacted deal, and act on that rather than on what you would do directly.
Wiifm: Advising on a deal you cannot execute is a different job from running one. Being clear about which levers you hold saves arguing over the ones you do not.
DesiredOutcome: The commercial structure tested, the levers you genuinely hold separated from the ones the partner holds, and one specific piece of enablement prepared.

RoleTopicName: Spot Commercial Risk Across the Portfolio
RoleTopicDescription: Find the commercial exposure hiding in a portfolio of agreements too large to review individually, and decide which of it is worth acting on now.
TodayObjective: Identify the commercial risk in your book that will be expensive if it is found late.
Wiifm: Commercial problems in this segment are rarely dramatic. They are small, numerous, and discovered at renewal, when the options have gone.
DesiredOutcome: The portfolio scanned for commercial exposure, the highest-cost risk identified with evidence, and one intervention started.

RoleTopicName: Judge Which Engagement Signals Are Real
RoleTopicDescription: Work the Highly Engaged and program signals in your solution area, separate genuine buying intent from activity, and route each one before the window closes.
TodayObjective: Take the engagement signals in your solution area and decide, with evidence, which represent real intent and which do not.
Wiifm: Engagement data tells you someone clicked, not that someone is buying. Being able to tell the difference quickly is most of the job.
DesiredOutcome: Your solution-area signals separated into real intent, needs-more-evidence and noise, with one routed and the reasoning recorded.

RoleTopicName: Find Where Your Solution Area Actually Lands
RoleTopicDescription: Work out where your solution area has genuine propensity across the territories you support, test that against real engagement evidence, and decide where your own time goes rather than spreading it evenly.
TodayObjective: Identify the accounts where your solution area has both propensity and evidence, and separate them from the ones that only have propensity.
Wiifm: Propensity models will happily hand you a long list. The ones that convert are the ones where something has already happened, and telling those apart early is most of the job.
DesiredOutcome: A short list of accounts with both propensity and engagement evidence, the difference explained, and one taken into the qualification progression.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation for Digital Solution Specialists
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session motion, where AI reduces the research and triage load across a solution area spanning several territories, and what to bring back each week.
TodayObjective: Understand how the DSS path runs and where the human checkpoints protect solution and qualification judgment.
Wiifm: You cover a solution area across more territories than you can hold in your head. This is about spending your time where it changes an outcome.
DesiredOutcome: DSSs know how the motion works, which tools may show up, and what to try before the next session.

RoleTopicName: Bring Solution Depth to a Conversation You Did Not Arrange
RoleTopicDescription: Prepare for a customer conversation the DAE owns, where you are there for solution depth and have limited context on the relationship.
TodayObjective: Prepare to add solution value in a conversation somebody else scoped and will lead.
Wiifm: Being pulled into a customer conversation at short notice is the job. Turning up informed rather than improvising is what makes the DAE bring you back.
DesiredOutcome: The solution-area contribution prepared, the customer's likely technical objection anticipated, and the boundary with the DAE agreed.

RoleTopicName: Move the Solution Decision, Not the Deal
RoleTopicDescription: Advance the part of a deal that belongs to your solution area, and be clear about where your influence ends and the DAE's ownership begins.
TodayObjective: Identify the solution decision blocking one opportunity and take it forward without taking over the deal.
Wiifm: Specialists lose credibility by either hovering or bulldozing. Knowing exactly which decision is yours is what makes you useful on the next one.
DesiredOutcome: The solution decision named, the evidence it needs assembled, and one action taken inside your own remit.

RoleTopicName: Prove the Solution Did What You Said It Would
RoleTopicDescription: Evidence the outcome your solution area promised, across the accounts where it was deployed, so the next conversation starts from proof rather than from the pitch.
TodayObjective: Find the accounts where your solution area can be evidenced, and the ones where it cannot.
Wiifm: A specialist who can point at a comparable customer wins the next conversation before it starts. That evidence has to be collected before you need it.
DesiredOutcome: Solution-area outcomes separated into evidenced and unevidenced, with one reusable proof point assembled.

RoleTopicName: Align Customer Investment to Account Strategy and Opportunity Outcomes
RoleTopicDescription: Connect customer investment to a live account priority or deal barrier without implying eligibility, funding, or approval.
TodayObjective: Identify where customer investment could remove a decision, deployment, or adoption barrier and name the next governed action.
Wiifm: You are often the first to see the barrier. Naming where investment could unlock the decision helps you start the right conversation without overstepping ownership.
DesiredOutcome: An investment hypothesis tied to an account or opportunity, with evidence, open questions, accountable owner, and next human decision.

RoleTopicName: Mobilize the Account Team and Partners Around the Opportunity
RoleTopicDescription: Make role coverage, handoffs, partner fit, and follow-through explicit for a live account or opportunity.
TodayObjective: Turn a matrixed account motion into clear roles, handoffs, and partner actions that move the next customer decision.
Wiifm: AEs lead through influence. When ownership is explicit, less time is spent chasing context and more time is spent advancing the customer decision.
DesiredOutcome: A role and partner orchestration plan with missing roles, owners, inputs, dates, and follow-up rhythm named.

RoleTopicName: Lead a Customer QBR and Executive Value Cadence
RoleTopicDescription: Turn outcomes, usage, commitments, investments, risks, and expansion plays into an executive-ready customer value cadence.
TodayObjective: Build a customer-ready value and QBR narrative that connects what happened to what the customer should decide next.
Wiifm: Value that is not evidenced is opinion. Value that is not communicated is invisible, especially before renewals and expansion conversations.
DesiredOutcome: An executive value and QBR brief with supported outcomes, open commitments, risks, expansion plays, and strategic asks.

RoleTopicName: Assess the Strategic and Technical Case for Investment
RoleTopicDescription: Test a proposed investment against the account technology strategy, deployment readiness, consumption path, and role boundaries.
TodayObjective: Decide whether this investment is worth your technical time, or whether it only looks strategic.
Wiifm: Investment that does not move the technology strategy still consumes technical time. Testing fit early is cheaper.
DesiredOutcome: A strategic and technical investment assessment with dependencies, readiness, risks, and the next governed decision named.

RoleTopicName: Prepare the Technical Contribution for a Customer Business Review
RoleTopicDescription: Contribute the strategic technical narrative, roadmap, key technical decisions, risks, and evidence to a customer business review.
TodayObjective: Bring the technical strategy into the customer value conversation.
Wiifm: Customer business reviews miss value when technical decisions, proof, and roadmap dependencies are absent or disconnected.
DesiredOutcome: A technical CBR contribution with roadmap points, evidence, risks, decisions, and follow-through.

RoleTopicName: Assess Technical Health and Prioritize Risk Response
RoleTopicDescription: Connect strategic and technical risks to account priorities and specialist alignment.
TodayObjective: Find the technical risk that most threatens the account strategy and decide what to do about it.
Wiifm: Risk found early is a conversation. The same risk found late is an escalation.
DesiredOutcome: A prioritized technical risk response with source signals, owner, intervention, and checkpoint.

RoleTopicName: Scope an Investment-Funded Technical Proof with Success Criteria
RoleTopicDescription: Bound the technical scope, proof evidence, success measures, failure modes, and delivery handoff for investment-funded work.
TodayObjective: Agree what would count as proof before the work starts, rather than after someone disputes the result.
Wiifm: Investment-funded work underdelivers when the technical proof is vague. SEs create leverage by bounding the scope before work starts.
DesiredOutcome: A technical scope, success-measure package, failure-mode register, and delivery handoff with open decisions named.

RoleTopicName: Clarify Commercial, Policy, and Approval Dependencies for Customer Investment
RoleTopicDescription: Surface the commercial structure, policy, agreement, exception, and approval dependencies an investment request will encounter.
TodayObjective: Name the commercial and approval dependencies before the investment request reaches review.
Wiifm: Investment requests lose time when commercial dependencies are discovered late. Naming the questions and owners early avoids rework without implying approval authority.
DesiredOutcome: A dependency and approval map with authoritative questions, owners, unresolved evidence, and the next human decision.

RoleTopicName: Validate Delivery Readiness and Technical Outcome Measures
RoleTopicDescription: Test whether investment-funded scope can be delivered as written, against dependencies, prerequisites, and technical checkpoints.
TodayObjective: Test whether the investment can actually be delivered as scoped.
Wiifm: You will be delivering it. Readiness gaps found now are gaps you do not absorb later.
DesiredOutcome: A delivery-readiness assessment with dependencies, prerequisites, and technical checkpoints defined.

RoleTopicName: Govern Customer Investment Execution and Value Realization
RoleTopicDescription: Govern investment execution, handoffs, and value evidence as part of the success plan rather than as a side process.
TodayObjective: Run customer investment as part of the success plan, not as a side process.
Wiifm: Customer investment only creates trust when execution, handoffs, and value evidence are governed from the start.
DesiredOutcome: An investment execution rhythm with owners, checkpoints, risks, and the evidence needed for the realization review.

RoleTopicName: Align Partner and Specialist Support to Technical Priorities
RoleTopicDescription: Identify where partner or specialist capacity is needed to advance the technical decision path.
TodayObjective: Make partner and specialist involvement match the technical priority, not the org chart.
Wiifm: Technical strategy often stalls because the right expertise is not involved at the right time.
DesiredOutcome: A partner and specialist alignment plan with capability gaps, owners, timing, and next decision.

RoleTopicName: Develop and Advance an Investment Request
RoleTopicDescription: Assemble request readiness, contributor coordination, partner and supplier inputs, and status follow-through into an investment request a reviewer can act on.
TodayObjective: Get an investment request from idea to review-ready without rework or overstated approval status.
Wiifm: You often own the request path. Most delay comes from missing inputs, unclear ownership, or hidden open questions.
DesiredOutcome: A request package a reviewer can act on, with confirmed inputs, gaps, owners, and next governed action.

RoleTopicName: Identify and Test an AI-Assisted Workflow
RoleTopicDescription: Bring a recurring workflow the team already owns, make its friction visible, and design one bounded experiment to test this week.
TodayObjective: Choose one real recurring workflow the team already owns, find the smallest step AI could assist, and leave with one bounded experiment and a named owner.
Wiifm: You practice on your own work rather than a worked example, so what you leave with is already relevant to your accounts. It works for any role and any workflow, so the team can run it again without new content.
DesiredOutcome: One workflow selected, one assistable step identified, one bounded experiment designed with a human checkpoint, and one person accountable for bringing evidence back.

RoleTopicName: Find the Deal Facts Before You Need Them
RoleTopicDescription: Use the deal-making capabilities in Sales Agent to retrieve what is in a customer's agreement, what they own, what is expiring, and what has been discounted.
TodayObjective: Learn how to retrieve real agreement, enrollment, and consumption facts for one of your own accounts, and recognize where the work stops being yours.
Wiifm: Every role touches a deal without owning it. You stop waiting on someone else for answers that take ninety seconds to retrieve, and you stop walking into customer conversations without knowing what the customer already bought.
DesiredOutcome: One account looked up for real, the facts that surprised you named, and a clear line drawn between what you can answer yourself and what belongs to the deal owner.

RoleTopicName: Read the Customer Satisfaction Signal and Intervene Early
RoleTopicDescription: Use the satisfaction, support and relationship signals the customer has already given us to find the accounts most likely to escalate, and act while the conversation is still yours to lead.
TodayObjective: Find the account whose satisfaction signal is deteriorating fastest and decide the intervention before the customer raises it.
Wiifm: You usually hear about a dissatisfied customer from your manager or from the customer. Both are late. This is the version where you hear it first.
DesiredOutcome: A ranked view of satisfaction risk across your accounts, with the evidence behind each, one owned intervention, and the escalation threshold that would change who is involved.

RoleTopicName: Take On an Account Without Making the Customer Start Over
RoleTopicDescription: Work a live account transition end to end, from reading what you inherited through to the customer meeting and the ninety-day follow-up.
TodayObjective: Take one account you are inheriting or handing over and get it to the point where the customer conversation can happen with confidence.
Wiifm: Every seller inherits accounts, and every seller has inherited a bad one. This is the session where you decide which kind you are about to hand someone else.
DesiredOutcome: One transition moved forward with the inherited context understood, the gaps named, the customer conversation prepared, and the follow-up owned.

RoleTopicName: Make the Handoff Land Where It Is Received
RoleTopicDescription: Prepare, run and close a handoff between roles so the receiving team can act on it the same day rather than reconstructing it.
TodayObjective: Take one live opportunity or milestone you are handing over or receiving, and get it to the point where the receiving role could act without asking you a question.
Wiifm: You have received a handoff that told you nothing, and you have probably sent one. This is the session where the difference becomes visible.
DesiredOutcome: One handoff prepared or repaired, with the qualification documented, the milestone detail complete, and the receiving role able to act.

RoleTopicName: Build the Consumption Plan the Customer Will Actually Follow
RoleTopicDescription: Turn a customer commitment into a sequenced consumption plan with owned milestones, dependencies and evidence that deployment is real.
TodayObjective: Take one committed customer and produce or repair the consumption plan that turns their commitment into deployed, used workloads.
Wiifm: You are accountable for the technical plan behind the number. This is where that plan becomes something the v-team can execute rather than a forecast you defend.
DesiredOutcome: A consumption plan with sequenced milestones, named owners, dependencies and the evidence that will show each milestone is genuinely progressing.

RoleTopicName: Find Out Whether Your Executive Relationships Are Real
RoleTopicDescription: Test the stakeholder map against evidence, find where sponsorship is assumed rather than established, and take one action that deepens it.
TodayObjective: Take one account and establish honestly which executive relationships would hold under pressure and which only exist on the map.
Wiifm: Everyone has an account where the sponsor left and nobody noticed for a quarter. This is how you find that before it costs you.
DesiredOutcome: A tested stakeholder picture with the assumed relationships separated from the evidenced ones, and one action owned to deepen the relationship that matters most.

RoleTopicName: Pressure-Test the Territory Plan Before Someone Else Does
RoleTopicDescription: Work the arithmetic behind your territory and coverage plan, find where it does not add up, and prepare the support request that closes the gap.
TodayObjective: Establish whether your territory plan actually covers your number, and name the gap before a review does.
Wiifm: You will be asked to defend this plan. Better to find its weakest assumption yourself, while there is still time to do something about it.
DesiredOutcome: A coverage gap quantified against quota, the assumptions it rests on named, and a specific, evidenced support ask.

RoleTopicName: Make Your Best Work Reusable by Someone Else
RoleTopicDescription: Take something you built that worked, and package it so a colleague can find it, trust it and adapt it without asking you.
TodayObjective: Turn one thing you have already built into an asset another person could pick up and use without you in the room.
Wiifm: You have rebuilt something a colleague had already solved, and someone has rebuilt yours. This is the half hour that stops that happening again.
DesiredOutcome: One reusable asset with its purpose, prerequisites, limitations and owner recorded, stored where someone would actually look for it.

RoleTopicName: Drive Committed Milestones Through to Realized Usage
RoleTopicDescription: Take the milestones the customer has committed to and drive them through delivery to usage the customer would defend, rather than to a completion flag.
TodayObjective: Take one committed milestone and establish whether it is genuinely progressing to usage, then own the intervention if it is not.
Wiifm: You inherit committed milestones and are measured on their completion. This is where you find out early which ones are quietly not going to land.
DesiredOutcome: A read on each committed milestone showing evidence of real progress, the ones at risk named with a cause, and one intervention owned.

RoleTopicName: Get an Uncommitted Milestone Ready for the Customer to Commit
RoleTopicDescription: Test an uncommitted milestone against what a customer commitment actually requires, and close the gaps that would make the commitment fail.
TodayObjective: Take one uncommitted milestone and establish whether the sponsor, outcome, value and budget behind it are real enough to commit.
Wiifm: Milestones that get committed on optimism come back as your missed number. This is where you find out which ones are actually ready.
DesiredOutcome: A read on each uncommitted milestone against the commitment criteria, the failing criteria named, and one milestone taken forward or deliberately held.

RoleTopicName: Confirm the Technical Basis Before a Milestone Is Committed
RoleTopicDescription: Establish whether the technical path, the dependencies and the delivery model behind a milestone will hold before anyone commits to its date.
TodayObjective: Take one uncommitted milestone and separate what is technically confirmed from what is assumed, before the date becomes a commitment.
Wiifm: You are the person who knows whether the date is achievable. This is the half hour where saying so still changes the outcome.
DesiredOutcome: A technical readiness position on one milestone with the confirmed facts, the open assumptions, the dependencies and a commit or hold recommendation.

RoleTopicName: Land the Fiscal Year Without Damaging Next Year
RoleTopicDescription: Separate what is genuinely pinned to the fiscal calendar from what only feels urgent, and act on the part that is real while there is still time.
TodayObjective: Establish what can still book this fiscal year, what has to be corrected before the systems close, and what should be left on its own clock.
Wiifm: The costly year-end mistakes are a record nobody fixed in time and a deal that was forced early and discounted for no reason. Both are avoidable and both are decided now.
DesiredOutcome: A list of what can still book with the runway it needs, the records to correct before cutoff, and the deals you have deliberately left in the new year.

RoleTopicName: Keep Pinned-Partner Deals Moving Between Stages
RoleTopicDescription: Track where your pinned-partner deals actually sit across the co-sell stages, find the ones that have stopped moving, and use the partner rhythm to unblock them.
TodayObjective: Establish where your pinned-partner deals are stuck and take one of them into the next partner conversation with a specific ask.
Wiifm: Partner deals stall between stages rather than failing outright, and nobody raises it because it is nobody's obvious job. It is yours.
DesiredOutcome: A stage-by-stage read on your pinned-partner deals, the stalled ones identified with a likely cause, and one specific ask prepared for the partner.

RoleTopicName: Work a Consumption Portfolio You Cannot Cover Account by Account
RoleTopicDescription: Read consumption movement across a portfolio far larger than you can work individually, decide where your own time changes the outcome, and route the rest deliberately.
TodayObjective: Decide which handful of accounts get your own attention this month, and stop pretending the rest are covered.
Wiifm: At this coverage ratio the accounts you never reach are decided by default. This is how that becomes a choice instead.
DesiredOutcome: A triaged portfolio with the movement explained, a short list you are personally working, an explicit routing decision on the rest, and one intervention started.

RoleTopicName: Design Something a Partner Can Actually Build
RoleTopicDescription: Shape the technical solution knowing a partner will deliver it, engage them early enough to change the design, and write down what they need that you have been carrying in your head.
TodayObjective: Test one design against the person who will actually build it, rather than against your own understanding of it.
Wiifm: A design that only works when you explain it is not finished. This is where that gets found, while it is still cheap to change.
DesiredOutcome: One design tested for buildability by someone who was not in the discovery, with the assumptions written down and the partner questions answered before delivery starts.

RoleTopicName: Build a Joint Plan the Partner Will Actually Work
RoleTopicDescription: Assess what a partner can genuinely deliver rather than what they have agreed to, build the joint plan inside the data rules that govern partner exchange, and set the trigger that tells you the plan has stopped being true.
TodayObjective: Test one joint plan against partner capacity and incentive rather than against partner intent.
Wiifm: Partners agree to plans in the meeting and work the deals that pay them. A plan that ignores that is a plan you will be explaining at the quarterly review.
DesiredOutcome: A joint plan tested against capacity and incentive, the data-sharing boundary respected, and a named trigger for revisiting it.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-week huddle motion: why Frontier Accelerator exists, what happens in a thirty-minute huddle, the five roles that make it work, and what is expected of you between sessions.
TodayObjective: Understand how the huddle motion runs, what you are being asked to do each week, and where your own judgment stays yours.
Wiifm: You are Customer Zero. Before we ask a customer to put AI at the center of how they work, we do it on our own work and find out honestly where it helps and where it does not. The aim is to get time back from the assembling, and to find out first-hand where AI earns that time and where it does not.
DesiredOutcome: You know how the motion works, what happens in each huddle, what is expected of you between sessions, and you leave with one thing to try before the next one.

RoleTopicName: Find Out What Has Already Been Discovered
RoleTopicDescription: Establish what the partner, the DAE and the specialist already know before you start asking, so the customer is not taken through the same questions twice.
TodayObjective: Work out what discovery has already happened and what only you can establish.
Wiifm: Asking a customer something a partner asked them last week makes the whole team look uncoordinated, and it costs you the goodwill you needed for the hard questions.
DesiredOutcome: A clear read on what is already known, what is only assumed, and the short list of things that genuinely need you rather than repeating discovery somebody has already done.

RoleTopicName: Prove It Without Building It Again
RoleTopicDescription: Decide the smallest proof that would settle the decision, and reach for something that already exists before building anything bespoke.
TodayObjective: Settle one customer's technical doubt without building a proof from scratch.
Wiifm: A bespoke proof per customer does not scale to the number of customers you cover. The engineers who keep up are the ones who reuse.
DesiredOutcome: The decision the proof must settle named, an existing asset found or ruled out, and the smallest sufficient proof scoped.

RoleTopicName: Answer a Question You Were Not Asked Directly
RoleTopicDescription: Handle a technical question relayed to you by a partner or a seller, where you are not in the room and your answer will be passed on in your absence.
TodayObjective: Answer one relayed technical question in a form that survives being repeated by somebody else.
Wiifm: Your answer gets forwarded, pasted and paraphrased. Writing it for the person who will relay it, rather than for yourself, is what stops it arriving wrong.
DesiredOutcome: The real question established, an answer written to survive relay, and the parts that must not be paraphrased marked.

RoleTopicName: Find the Problem Before the Customer Does
RoleTopicDescription: Locate the customers running a configuration you already know is fragile, and get the fix moving through whoever actually operates it.
TodayObjective: Identify which of your customers are exposed to a technical problem you have already seen elsewhere.
Wiifm: You will not find these by inspection, because you do not operate any of it and there are too many. You find them by recognizing the pattern you have already met.
DesiredOutcome: The exposed customers identified, the ones whose partner already knows separated out, and one fix routed to whoever operates it.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-week huddle motion: why Frontier Accelerator exists, what happens in a thirty-minute huddle, the five roles that make it work, and what is expected of you between sessions.
TodayObjective: Understand how the huddle motion runs, what you are being asked to do each week, and where your own judgment stays yours.
Wiifm: You are Customer Zero. Before we ask a customer to put AI at the center of how they work, we do it on our own work and find out honestly where it helps and where it does not. The aim is to get time back from the assembling, and to find out first-hand where AI earns that time and where it does not.
DesiredOutcome: You know how the motion works, what happens in each huddle, what is expected of you between sessions, and you leave with one thing to try before the next one.

RoleTopicName: Get Technical Work Done by People You Do Not Manage
RoleTopicDescription: Hand technical work to a delivery partner with enough for them to act, and set up a way of knowing whether it landed, without a support agreement or an escalation path behind you.
TodayObjective: Hand one piece of technical work to a partner in a form they can act on without you.
Wiifm: On these accounts there is no Unified agreement and no funded delivery. If the partner cannot act on what you gave them, nothing happens at all.
DesiredOutcome: One technical handover a partner can act on unaided, with a named signal that would tell you whether it worked.

RoleTopicName: Make the One Conversation Count
RoleTopicDescription: Prepare for a technical conversation you may not get to repeat, and leave the customer with something that keeps working after you have moved on to the next account.
TodayObjective: Prepare one customer conversation on the assumption that it is the only one you will get.
Wiifm: At this coverage you are not building a relationship, you are making a single intervention. What you leave behind matters more than what you say.
DesiredOutcome: A conversation prepared around one decision, with something durable left behind and the next owner named.

RoleTopicName: Evidence an Outcome Somebody Else Delivered
RoleTopicDescription: Work out what can honestly be claimed about technical outcomes when a partner did the delivery and there is no support engagement record to draw on.
TodayObjective: Establish what your portfolio can actually evidence, and get it to the people who need it at renewal.
Wiifm: Without a Unified engagement there is no delivery record behind you. If you do not capture the evidence, the renewal conversation happens without it.
DesiredOutcome: Outcomes separated into evidenced, partner-held and unevidenced, with the evidenced ones passed to whoever owns the renewal.

RoleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
RoleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-week huddle motion: why Frontier Accelerator exists, what happens in a thirty-minute huddle, the five roles that make it work, and what is expected of you between sessions.
TodayObjective: Understand how the huddle motion runs, what you are being asked to do each week, and where your own judgment stays yours.
Wiifm: You are Customer Zero. Before we ask a customer to put AI at the center of how they work, we do it on our own work and find out honestly where it helps and where it does not. The aim is to get time back from the assembling, and to find out first-hand where AI earns that time and where it does not.
DesiredOutcome: You know how the motion works, what happens in each huddle, what is expected of you between sessions, and you leave with one thing to try before the next one.

RoleTopicName: Work the Demand Coming the Other Way
RoleTopicDescription: Handle opportunity that originates with a partner and arrives at Microsoft, where the qualification you can do is limited and the clock is already running.
TodayObjective: Take one partner-originated opportunity and establish whether it is real before the window closes on it.
Wiifm: Everyone else pushes work out to partners. You also receive it, and what arrives is qualified to the partner's standard rather than to yours.
DesiredOutcome: Partner-originated opportunities separated by what can actually be verified, with one progressed and the registration requirements checked.

RoleTopicName: Run a Rhythm Across More Partners Than You Can Meet
RoleTopicDescription: Decide which partners get your time this month and what each meeting is actually for, when the commitment is a minimum cadence per partner seller.
TodayObjective: Decide which partners get your attention this month and which get a lighter touch, deliberately.
Wiifm: A cadence obligation across a portfolio becomes a calendar full of status meetings unless somebody decides what each one is for.
DesiredOutcome: Your partner portfolio triaged for the month, with the meetings that need an agenda separated from the ones that need only a check-in.

RoleTopicName: Find Out What Happened After the Partner Closed It
RoleTopicDescription: Close the visibility gap that opens once a partner transacts and delivers, because you are the only route Microsoft has back to what the customer actually got.
TodayObjective: Establish what is known about outcomes at customers your partners closed, and what only the partner can tell you.
Wiifm: Once a partner closes and delivers, Microsoft largely stops seeing the customer. If you do not ask, nobody finds out until the renewal.
DesiredOutcome: The visibility gap mapped across recent partner-closed deals, with one partner asked directly about outcomes.

RoleTopicName: Check the Rules Before the Structure Hardens
RoleTopicDescription: Run a deal against the policy, licensing and eligibility questions it will eventually meet, at a point where the answer can still change the shape.
TodayObjective: Find the policy question on one live deal that would be expensive to discover at approval.
Wiifm: Policy questions found at approval cost weeks. Found now they cost a conversation, and you are the only person on the deal who will think to ask.
DesiredOutcome: One deal checked against the questions it will face, with every unresolved item routed to the authoritative owner rather than guessed.

RoleTopicName: Prepare the Negotiation You May Not Be In
RoleTopicDescription: Set the concession logic and authority boundaries for a negotiation that a partner may actually conduct, so the limits hold when you are not in the room.
TodayObjective: Set the concession boundary on one deal before anyone is under pressure to move it.
Wiifm: A boundary defined in the room is defined under pressure by whoever is least able to be objective about it. Yours has to survive being applied by someone else.
DesiredOutcome: Concession logic and authority limits written down, with the escalation trigger named and the partner briefed on what they cannot concede.

RoleTopicName: Get the Approvals Moving When You Do Not Own the Deal
RoleTopicDescription: Route commercial approvals and execution steps to named owners on a deal where the partner transacts and several of the steps are not yours to take.
TodayObjective: Replace every implied approval owner on one deal with a named one.
Wiifm: Approvals discovered one at a time cost a week each. At this book size nobody is going to map them for you, and the partner cannot.
DesiredOutcome: The approval path mapped with a named owner and required evidence for each step, and the steps that belong to the partner identified as theirs.

RoleTopicName: Make the Commercial Case Reviewable
RoleTopicDescription: Turn an agreed commercial structure into a narrative an approver or a customer executive can inspect and act on, in a segment where you will usually not be in the room to explain it.
TodayObjective: Turn one commercial structure into a narrative that can be approved without you present.
Wiifm: Commercial logic that only lives in your head cannot be approved by anyone else. Through a partner, you are not there to explain it.
DesiredOutcome: A commercial narrative that states the decision being asked for, traces every figure to a source, names its assumptions, and sets out the approval route.

RoleTopicName: Design Something That Will Run Without You There
RoleTopicDescription: Shape a deployment-ready architecture for a customer you will not be on site for, where a partner or the customer's own team does the building and nobody has premier support to fall back on.
TodayObjective: Take one design and make it survivable by the people who will actually operate it.
Wiifm: A design that needs you present to work is a design that fails the week you move to the next account. At this portfolio size you are never coming back.
DesiredOutcome: One architecture tested against who will build it, who will run it, and what happens when it breaks with nobody senior in the room.

RoleTopicName: Find the Technical Problem Before It Reaches the Number
RoleTopicDescription: Work technical health across a portfolio too large to inspect account by account, and decide which risk is worth your time while it is still cheap to fix.
TodayObjective: Find the technical risk in your portfolio that will be expensive if it is found late, and start on it.
Wiifm: Consumption falling is the last signal you get, not the first. By the time it shows in the number, the technical cause is months old and the customer has already worked around you.
DesiredOutcome: The portfolio scanned for technical risk, the most costly one identified with evidence, and a standing check set up so the next one reaches you sooner.

RoleTopicName: Find the Next Workload Inside the One That Works
RoleTopicDescription: Use deployment and usage evidence to identify the workload a customer is genuinely ready for, rather than the one that is easiest to propose.
TodayObjective: Test one expansion idea against what the customer is actually succeeding with.
Wiifm: The best expansion signal you will ever get is a workload the customer is already running well. Everything else is a pitch, and at this volume pitches do not scale.
DesiredOutcome: One evidenced expansion hypothesis with the readiness signal named, handed to whoever owns the commercial conversation.

RoleTopicName: Stop Rebuilding What You Already Built
RoleTopicDescription: Turn work you have already done into something a colleague can pick up without asking you first, in a segment where the same technical problem arrives repeatedly across different customers.
TodayObjective: Capture one thing you built so another engineer could use it unaided.
Wiifm: At this volume, rebuilding what exists is the single most expensive habit available to you. The same question is being answered from scratch across the team every week.
DesiredOutcome: One reusable asset captured with enough context that somebody who was not there can tell whether it fits their situation.

RoleTopicName: Close the Partner Capability Gap That Is Holding a Deal
RoleTopicDescription: Find where a partner's technical confidence is what is actually stopping a partner-led opportunity, and close that gap rather than doing the work for them.
TodayObjective: Find one partner technical gap that is blocking progress and start closing it.
Wiifm: When a partner-led opportunity stalls, partner technical confidence is a cause worth testing before you look at the product. Doing the work yourself closes this deal and leaves the same gap open for the next one.
DesiredOutcome: One partner capability gap named with evidence, and an enablement action owned and dated rather than absorbed by you.

RoleTopicName: Build a Competitive Position the Customer Would Recognize
