RoleTopicDescription: Work out where your solution area genuinely wins against what the customer is actually comparing it to, and where it does not.
TodayObjective: Test one competitive position against the customer's real decision criteria rather than against a feature list.
Wiifm: A differentiator the customer does not value is a feature, not an advantage. At this volume you will not get a second meeting to correct the framing.
DesiredOutcome: A competitive position the customer would recognize, where differentiation is evidenced, genuine gaps are named rather than defended, and the objections you will actually meet are prepared.

RoleTopicName: Make the Ask Specific Enough to Be Accepted
RoleTopicDescription: Mobilize the technical, partner or funding support an opportunity needs, in a segment where nobody is assigned to your deal and every ask competes with someone else's.
TodayObjective: Turn one vague support need into a specific ask with a named owner and a date.
Wiifm: A vague ask gets a vague response two weeks later. You have no v-team and no assigned specialists, so how you ask is most of whether you get it.
DesiredOutcome: One support ask made specific, sent to a named person, with a date and a standing check on whether it was answered.

RoleTopicName: Confirm the Partner Has the Capacity to Deliver
RoleTopicDescription: Assess whether a partner has the capability and the capacity to deliver what is being routed to them, before the customer finds out they do not.
TodayObjective: Find the capability or capacity gap most likely to stall partner-led delivery, and name what closing it would take.
Wiifm: Routing work to a partner who cannot deliver it damages the customer and the partner at once, and you will be the one who chose them.
DesiredOutcome: A readiness view where demonstrated capability is separated from asserted capacity, one gap is named, and the closing action carries an owner and a date.

RoleTopicName: Have the Conversation in the Partner's Economics
RoleTopicDescription: Prepare the partner conversation that changes behavior, grounded in what the partner's business actually gains rather than in what Microsoft needs.
TodayObjective: Prepare one partner conversation framed in the partner's own economics with a specific ask.
Wiifm: Partners act on their business case, not on our targets. A conversation framed in Microsoft priorities gets agreement in the room and nothing afterwards.
DesiredOutcome: A partner conversation brief in the partner's terms, with one specific ask and the likely objections prepared.

RoleTopicName: Choose the Investment Route Before You Build the Case
RoleTopicDescription: Work out which investment route a solution-area opportunity actually qualifies for, before spending effort on a request that was never going to fit.
TodayObjective: Match one opportunity to the investment route it genuinely qualifies for.
Wiifm: Picking the wrong investment vehicle means rebuilding the request against the right one. The selection takes an hour and the rebuild takes two weeks.
DesiredOutcome: One opportunity matched to a route, with the eligibility questions routed to their authoritative owner rather than assumed.

RoleTopicName: Use the Partner-Led Investment Routes Properly
RoleTopicDescription: Work the investment routes that run through partners rather than around them, which is where most SME&C investment actually sits.
TodayObjective: Match one partner opportunity to the partner-led investment route it qualifies for.
Wiifm: Most SME&C investment is partner-led by design. If you only know the direct route you are working the smallest part of what is available.
DesiredOutcome: One partner opportunity matched to a partner-led route, with the partner's own obligations under it made explicit to them.

RoleTopicName: Spot the Deal Where Investment Would Change the Answer
RoleTopicDescription: Recognize the account situations where customer investment is a genuine lever, and hand them to whoever owns the request.
TodayObjective: Identify one account where investment would change the outcome, and route it.
Wiifm: You see the barrier first and more often than anyone else. Recognizing the ones investment can move is most of the value you add here.
DesiredOutcome: One account identified where investment is a plausible lever, with the barrier evidenced and the request routed to its owner.

RoleTopicName: Define What an Investment-Funded Proof Must Show
RoleTopicDescription: Set the technical success and exit criteria for work that customer investment would fund, before it is requested.
TodayObjective: Define what one funded piece of technical work must demonstrate, observably.
Wiifm: You will be asked what the funded work proved. Deciding that before it starts is the difference between evidence and an argument.
DesiredOutcome: Observable success and exit criteria for one investment-funded piece of technical work.

RoleTopicName: Confirm the Customer Can Absorb the Funded Work
RoleTopicDescription: Check delivery readiness for work customer investment would fund, in an environment with no dedicated support relationship.
TodayObjective: Establish whether one customer could absorb funded technical work, and what would block it.
Wiifm: Funded work that stalls on a customer-side dependency is recorded as a Microsoft delivery failure, and you are the person who could have seen it coming.
DesiredOutcome: A readiness view for one funded engagement with the blocking dependencies named and owned.

RoleTopicName: Know Where Investment Meets Commercial Structure
RoleTopicDescription: Recognize where a customer investment interacts with commercial structure and precedent, in a segment where the CE does not own the investment request.
TodayObjective: Know what to look for when an investment appears on a deal you are structuring.
Wiifm: You will meet investment on deals you structure without owning the request. Knowing where it touches commercial precedent is the part that is yours.
DesiredOutcome: An understanding of where investment interacts with commercial structure, and what to raise when it does.

RoleTopicName: Check What Closed in Your Book
RoleTopicDescription: Review recent closed-won opportunities in your book and decide whether each record describes what actually happened.
TodayObjective: Work through recent closed-won records and decide which ones you can stand behind.
Wiifm: A closed record carries your number whether or not you set it, and one you cannot account for is still yours to explain.
DesiredOutcome: Recent closed-won opportunities reviewed against what you know, each classified as accounted for or questionable, and any questionable record acted on - or none found, and that recorded.

RoleTopicName: Protect Customer Satisfaction on the Delivery You Own
RoleTopicDescription: Read the satisfaction signals in a live delivery, decide which one would show up in the survey, and act on it while the delivery is still running.
TodayObjective: Find the thing this customer would mark you down for, and deal with it before they are asked.
Wiifm: A survey score arrives after you can do anything about it. The signals arrive while you still can.
DesiredOutcome: A satisfaction read where the risk is evidenced rather than felt, one action is owned, and anything belonging to another role has been routed rather than absorbed.

RoleTopicName: Become the Technical Advisor the Customer Asks For
RoleTopicDescription: Work out what this customer's roadmap will need you to be credible on next, compare that honestly against what you can speak to today, and close one gap.
TodayObjective: Name the one thing your customer will need you to know next that you could not defend today.
Wiifm: You get called in when you are the person who can answer. That list of topics is set by the customer's roadmap, not yours.
DesiredOutcome: A credibility position where the customer's next technical demand is named, the gap between that and what you can defend today is stated plainly, and one specific step to close it is owned.
